interactionPlan.concept: The Contrast Sensitivity Function (CSF) describes how our visual sensitivity to detail peaks at intermediate spatial frequencies and degrades at extreme frequencies or under optical blur.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand that human contrast sensitivity is band-pass, peaking at intermediate spatial frequencies rather than being uniform.
The student will be able to explain how optical blur or reduced illumination selectively degrades sensitivity to high spatial frequencies, shifting the threshold curve downward.
The student will be able to map abstract 'spatial frequency' to physical visual patterns of fine or coarse detail.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: Our eyes filter out both extremely coarse and extremely fine patterns, and physical factors like blur selectively erase our high-frequency detail vision first.

interactions.label: Optical Blur
interactions.effect: Smoothly morphs the sensitivity threshold curve from the red line (perfect vision, high frequency cutoff) to the blue line (blurred vision, reduced high frequency cutoff).
interactions.teaches: How optical blur acts as a low-pass filter, degrading high-spatial-frequency sensitivity while leaving low-frequency sensitivity unaffected.

interactions.label: Test Frequency
interactions.effect: Moves a vertical probe line across the X-axis and dynamically renders a visual sinusoidal grating panel illustrating that specific spatial frequency.
interactions.teaches: The physical meaning of 'spatial frequency' by directly connecting the logarithmic X-axis to a visible pattern of vertical stripes.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The visualization should contain a line plot with a logarithmic X-axis labeled 'log(frequency)' and a vertical Y-axis for 'Contrast Sensitivity Threshold'. It plots two main overlapping curve states: a red curve with a high-frequency cutoff, and a blue curve that droops significantly faster at high frequencies. A vertical dashed line indicates the selected test frequency. A dynamic preview window next to or below the plot displays a grayscale sine-wave grating corresponding to the selected frequency.
